title: Customs Assessment, Provisional Assessment and Adjudication

content.overview: Customs Assessment, Provisional Assessment and Adjudication. Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study:
Topic at a glance
Customs Assessment, Provisional Assessment and Adjudication is a registered theme in Taxation Laws. Customs Assessment, Provisional Assessment and Adjudication is governed by Income-tax Act, 2025; Income-tax Rules, 2026; CGST Act, 2017; IGST Act, 2017; applicable SGST Acts; and Customs Act, 1962, together with current rules, notifications and circulars. identify the tax period, charging statute, commencement date, amendment or notification in force, taxable event, jurisdictional notice and statutory appeal or writ route; use the Income-tax Act, 1961 only as historical transition/concordance where the 2025 Act applies.

Provenance, purpose and doctrinal foundation
The topic exists to organise a legally enforceable rule, doctrine or professional procedure. Read the statutory text, constitutional setting, institutional purpose and binding authorities together. The correct analysis begins with the legal question and avoids replacing the governing enactment with a generic textbook summary.

Textual anatomy and operative test
1. Identify the governing enactment, section, article, rule, doctrine or professional standard named by the topic.
2. Deconstruct definitions, conditions precedent, exceptions, provisos, explanations, jurisdictional limits and remedies.
3. Distinguish the topic from its nearest neighbour: Income-tax Act, 2025 — Structure, Commencement and Transition from the 1961 Act; Income-tax Rules, 2026 — Delegated Rules, Forms, Compliance and Procedure; Residential Status and Scope of Total Income.
4. Apply the rule to the record and state which fact satisfies or fails each ingredient.

Courtroom and evidentiary roadmap
Competent forum: the assessing authority, appellate authority, ITAT, GST appellate forum, High Court on a substantial question or constitutional writ jurisdiction, and Supreme Court according to the statute. the assessee and Revenue bear burdens according to the charging provision, exemption or deduction claimed, assessment record, statutory presumption and appellate issue. Where electronic records are relied upon, apply BSA 2023 s. 63 and the applicable burden provisions without treating electronic admissibility as proof of the ultimate fact. Identify limitation, notice, maintainability, alternative remedy and the exact relief sought.
